genZNote: The 'seal-like barking cough' description in every textbook exists because of this virus specifically.

morphology.shape: Pleomorphic, enveloped virion with helical nucleocapsid

habitat.hostAssociation: Infects the respiratory epithelium, particularly the upper airway and larynx/trachea in young children

identificationClues: Diagnosed by a respiratory viral PCR panel, which has largely replaced viral culture and antigen testing
Classic cause of croup (laryngotracheobronchitis) in young children — a seal-like barking cough with inspiratory stridor
'Steeple sign' — subglottic narrowing seen on anteroposterior neck X-ray in croup, a classic radiographic finding
Serotype 1 is the most common cause of croup, typically in fall; serotype 3 more often causes bronchiolitis/pneumonia in infants

diseases: Croup (laryngotracheobronchitis) — the leading viral cause, with a barking cough, hoarseness, and inspiratory stridor
Bronchiolitis and pneumonia, particularly in infants and immunocompromised patients
Upper respiratory tract infection (common cold-like illness)
clinicalImportance.transmission: Respiratory droplets and contact with contaminated surfaces/fomites
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: A major cause of pediatric respiratory illness worldwide, with seasonal patterns varying by serotype (type 1 classically causes fall croup outbreaks); a significant cause of severe respiratory disease in immunocompromised and stem cell transplant patients
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Multiplex respiratory viral PCR panels now provide same-day identification and help distinguish parainfluenza from RSV, influenza, and other respiratory viruses with overlapping presentations

examFacts.keyBiochemicalReaction: Not applicable — diagnosed by respiratory PCR panel
examFacts.importantTest: Respiratory viral PCR panel; steeple sign on neck X-ray supports the clinical diagnosis of croup
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: The leading cause of childhood croup, producing the classic barking cough and the 'steeple sign' of subglottic narrowing on neck X-ray
